title: What drug and alcohol training does CASA Part 99 require for aviation workers in Australia?
seoTitle: CASA Part 99 DAMP education and training
description: CASR Part 99 DAMP education explained: who must have a DAMP, the employee and supervisor program content, the 30 month refresh, reporting and records.
shortAnswer: Under Part 99 of the Civil Aviation Safety Regulations 1998, Australian aviation organizations whose staff perform safety sensitive aviation activities must have a drug and alcohol management plan (DAMP) that includes an education program. Employees must be made aware of the policy, workplace testing, support services and aviation safety risks, and DAMP supervisors must be trained to manage problematic use. Both groups attend before starting duties and then within 30 months of their last attendance.
keyTakeaways: Regulation 99.030 requires a DAMP from AOC holders, Part 145 maintenance organizations, Part 141 flying training operators, aerodrome certificate holders, air traffic service providers, screening authorities and other listed organizations that have staff performing safety sensitive aviation activities.
The drug and alcohol education program defined in regulation 99.010 has four awareness components for employees and a separate education and training component for DAMP supervisors.
Regulation 99.080 requires attendance before starting duties as an employee or supervisor, and again within 30 months of the person's last attendance.

DAMP organizations report education attendance to CASA for each six month period ending before 1 March and 1 September, within 21 days, and keep the underlying records for 5 years (regulations 99.100 and 99.105).
Failing to have or review a DAMP is a strict liability offence carrying up to 50 penalty units under Subpart 99.B.
regulator: Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA), under Part 99 of the Civil Aviation Safety Regulations 1998 (CASR)
appliesTo: Air operator's certificate (AOC) holders, Part 141 flying training operators and Part 145 approved maintenance organizations
Aerodrome certificate holders, aviation rescue and fire fighting services, air traffic service providers and screening authorities
Employees, contractors, subcontractors and volunteers who perform safety sensitive aviation activities (SSAAs)
DAMP supervisors authorized to form an opinion on whether a person may be affected by drugs or alcohol

sections.heading: Which Australian aviation organizations must have a DAMP?

blocks.text: An organization needs a DAMP if it is on the list in regulation 99.030(2) and has an employee or contractor who performs, or is available to perform, a safety sensitive aviation activity (SSAA). Part 99 sits in Volume 3 of the [Civil Aviation Safety Regulations 1998](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F1998B00220/latest/text); this page reflects Compilation No. 103 of September 29, 2026, the current version as at November 2026.

items: AOC holders and production certificate holders.
Aerodrome certificate holders and approved aviation rescue and fire fighting services.
Air traffic service providers and training providers, and providers of aviation telecommunication and radionavigation services.
Part 145 organizations and holders of a certificate of approval under the Civil Aviation Regulations 1988.
Part 141 operators conducting flying training in aircraft.
Screening authorities under the Aviation Transport Security Regulations 2005.

blocks.text: Contractors count. An organization whose only SSAA workers are contracted staff, including a contractor's employees or subcontractors, still needs a DAMP that covers them. CASA's guidance says the education program is for all SSAA employees, "staff, contractors, subcontractors and volunteers".

sections.heading: What counts as a safety sensitive aviation activity?

blocks.text: Regulation 99.015 lists the SSAAs, and most of them apply even outside an aerodrome testing area. The scope is wider than flight crew and extends well into ground operations.

items: Any activity, other than as a passenger, in an aerodrome testing area.
Calculating the position of freight, baggage, passengers and fuel on aircraft.

Manufacturing or maintaining aircraft, aeronautical products, aviation radionavigation and telecommunication products, and reserve or emergency parachutes, and certifying that maintenance or issuing a certificate of release to service.
Fuelling and maintaining vehicles used to fuel aircraft on aerodrome testing areas.
Duties of airport security guards, screening officers, aircraft crew members, air traffic controllers and their supervisors.
Loading and driving baggage trolleys, providing flight information and search and rescue alert services, and aviation fire fighting.

blocks.text: Because load controllers, refuelers and baggage handlers are inside scope, a [training needs analysis](/guides/how-to-conduct-a-training-needs-analysis) based only on licensed roles will miss part of the population that must attend the education program.

sections.heading: What must the DAMP education program contain?

blocks.text: The program has two parts: awareness for SSAA employees and education and training for DAMP supervisors. Regulation 99.045 requires every DAMP to include the program, and regulation 99.010 defines its minimum content.

blocks.text: A DAMP supervisor is defined as a person with relevant training to form an opinion on whether someone may be adversely affected by a testable drug or under the influence of alcohol, and who is authorized for the reasonable grounds testing in paragraph 99.050(2)(c). The training is therefore what makes a reasonable grounds test lawful under the DAMP. Regulation 99.045(c) also requires the DAMP to identify each DAMP supervisor and the DAMP contact officer, with contact details.

sections.heading: When must employees and DAMP supervisors attend?

blocks.text: New SSAA employees and DAMP supervisors must attend before starting those duties, and everyone must attend again within 30 months of their last attendance. Regulation 99.080(1)(a) sets these timings.

CASA's guidance confirms the trigger covers both new employees and existing employees whose role changes to include SSAAs. Regulation 99.080 also requires the organization to tell each SSAA employee not to perform an SSAA while aware they are adversely affected, to encourage disclosure of alcohol or medication that may affect their work, to inform employees that testing requires a body sample, and to record DAMP policy and procedures under a controlled document protocol.

blocks.title: Setting the refresh date
blocks.text: The 30 month limit runs from each person's last attendance, not from a fixed organizational date. A tracker that resets per person avoids the common gap where a supervisor appointed mid cycle falls out of date. See [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: What must be reported to CASA and how long are records kept?

blocks.text: DAMP organizations report twice a year, including the number of SSAA employees who attended the education program for the first time and for a second or subsequent time. Regulation 99.100 defines the reporting periods as the six months before each 1 March and 1 September, and the report is due in writing within 21 days of the period ending.

items: Records used for the CASA report must be kept for 5 years from the date the information was given to CASA, in a secure location (regulation 99.105).
Within 6 months after the 5 years end, the records, or the parts relating to drug and alcohol test results, must be destroyed or deleted.
The DAMP must be reviewed every 5 years from the date it was developed and whenever CASA directs (regulation 99.085).
CASA may audit a DAMP organization and require records showing the DAMP was developed and implemented (regulation 99.090).

blocks.text: The mandatory destruction step is unusual among training record rules, so retention schedules that keep everything indefinitely are not compliant here. For the wider retention picture, see [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records).

sections.heading: Is there a simpler option for small aviation businesses?

blocks.text: Yes. CASA offers a micro-business exemption for DAMP organizations that do not provide scheduled air transport and have no more than 10 regular employees who are reasonably likely to perform SSAAs at least twice every 90 days.

An organization adopting it signs CASA's micro-business DAMP, and all SSAA employees and DAMP supervisors must complete CASA's alcohol and other drugs training. Within 14 days the organization must submit the signed DAMP and Form 008 naming its DAMP contact officer, and ensure the training is complete, keeping evidence of completion for audit. CASA's free eLearning has two modules, DAMP awareness for SSAA employees and DAMP supervisor training; it is compulsory under the micro-business exemption and recommended, not required, for other organizations.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each SSAA role and each 99.010 component to defined knowledge points before content is written, so the same structure drives the employee and supervisor modules, the 30 month refresh dates and the six monthly attendance counts reported to CASA.

faqs.q: Do contractors need to complete our DAMP education program?
faqs.a: Yes, if they perform or are available to perform an SSAA for your organization. Part 99 treats contractors, their employees and subcontractors as covered, and CASA's guidance names staff, contractors, subcontractors and volunteers. CASA also publishes separate exemptions for contracting other DAMP organizations or non-DAMP organizations.

faqs.q: Is CASA's free DAMP eLearning mandatory?
faqs.a: Only for organizations using the micro-business exemption. For all other DAMP organizations CASA recommends it as a base but does not require it. An organization that builds its own program must cover the employee and supervisor components defined in regulation 99.010.

faqs.q: What happens to staff who were employed before the organization's DAMP started?
faqs.a: Regulation 99.080 gave existing SSAA employees and DAMP supervisors six months from the commencement date to attend. After that, everyone follows the same rule: attend before starting SSAA or supervisor duties, then within 30 months of their last attendance.

faqs.q: Does Part 99 set a minimum length for DAMP training?
faqs.a: No. Unlike some United States transport rules, Part 99 sets content and timing but no minimum duration. Organizations should be able to show that each defined component was covered and understood, for example through an assessment or acknowledgment record.
